title: Gemini 4 Argon against Claude Opus 5.5
summary: Google's new frontier model leads its chosen rivals on the Vals Index and AutomationBench, and independent leaderboards confirm both. Its headline price of $2/$10 is introductory and doubles later; at the later price its cost per AutomationBench task is above Opus 5.5. Argon is open only to selected cyber partners, so no live test is possible yet.

observations.text: Argon is not generally available: access starts with selected cyber-defence partners, and Google has not published a public API model ID, so live tests are not possible yet.
Coding results are mixed: Argon leads DeepSWE v1.1 but trails GPT-6 Astra on FrontierSWE v2 (55.0% vs 65.5%) and Opus 5.5 on Terminal-bench 4.0 (57.4% vs 66.4%).
Google's comparison leaves out Claude Sonnet 5.5, which scores higher on Vibe Code Bench, and GPT-6.1 Sol, which already sells at the same $2/$10 price.
The headline 1 million tokens is an output limit, not input context; Google has not stated the commercial input limit.
Google ran Argon at its highest thinking setting, and some rows use unequal conditions, such as different video frame budgets on LVBench.

livePack.note: Runs the 15 starter tasks plus 7 multi-step efficiency tasks. Add tasks from your own work before trusting a verdict.

If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be 100 days from today? Answer with the day name only.
A shop gives 20% off, then a further 10% off the reduced price. What is the total discount as a percentage of the original price? Answer with the number only.
Which is the largest of these: 3/7, 0.45, 4/9, 0.43? Answer with the value exactly as written in the list.
Return only JSON with keys "po" and "total" (total as a number, in rupees) for this order: "PO-7781 for 12 units at Rs 1,250 each."
How many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) are in the word "transformation"? Answer with the number only.
